BLOCKER: `PurgeMonth` sets `purged_at` before deleting cold objects; if the delete fails, `audit_approve_purge` returns early on `purged_at IS NOT NULL`, leaving orphaned objects with no automated re-purge path — legally-required evidence destruction cannot be completed.

`architect_review.py` retry loop catches only `urllib.error.HTTPError`; `urllib.error.URLError` (DNS failure, connection reset, TCP timeout) propagates uncaught, defeating the retry mechanism precisely in the CI environments it targets.
MAJOR: `edpdata.AuditStore.Append` comment references "the audit_provision trigger" which was removed per AC; the empty section 10 in the migration and the dangling `audit_provision()` DROP in the down migration will mislead maintainers about the actual heal mechanism (catch-23514 + `audit_ensure_partitions`).

`architect_review.py` retry nudge says "previous attempt returned no content" even for HTTP 502/429 where the model never saw the prompt; the misleading context wastes tokens and may reduce review quality on retry.

EXCLUDE pattern change from `:(exclude)engineering/**` to `:(exclude,glob)**/engineering/**` broadens the exclusion from repo-root to any depth; changes under nested `engineering/` directories silently bypass review-sha computation.

`audit_archive_manifest` and `audit_partition_config` lack TRUNCATE revocations and statement-level deny triggers; a compromised `pf_owner` session can erase all archive/purge records with `TRUNCATE`, defeating the audit trail.

`pfaudit-swap close` records `swap_closed` before deleting the backup object with no duplicate-close guard; a failed delete leaves the dump in place but the state says closed, and a re-run attempts to re-record sign-off.
`edpsvc.checkAuditCoverage` emits metrics as raw JSON to stderr with no structured logging, no metrics endpoint, and no trace correlation — operationally invisible in standard monitoring pipelines.
MINOR: `DefaultSSE()` returns `"aws:kms"` when `PF_S3_BUCKET` is set without `PF_S3_KMS_KEY`, but `CheckSSE` always rejects this exact value; the two functions form an inherently contradictory contract in the common S3-without-KMS configuration.

`RestoreMonth` uses `fmt.Sprintf` to interpolate table names into SQL (`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS %s`, `CREATE TABLE %s LIKE %s`); inputs are validated but a `quoteIdentifier` helper would be safer and more maintainable.
`ArchiveKey` always returns a single shard (`part-000.ndjson`); very large months produce one multi-GB object that cannot be parallel-uploaded, with no sharding despite the naming suggesting it.
`audit_partitioned_id_seq` is orphaned after `Down` (renamed from `audit_id_seq` but never cleaned up); harmless but accumulates dead catalog objects over repeated swap/down cycles.
NIT: `architect_review.py` nudge text repeats the section-format instruction already in the system prompt, wasting tokens on every retry.
`audit_restore_lock` function name implies it acquires a lock; it only inserts an audit event — `audit_record_restore` would be clearer.
SUMMARY: The core swap, retention, hold-reconcile, and privilege-enforced hardening design is sound and well-tested, with catalog-driven crash recovery and bounded delta drain under lock. The top risks are the purge-before-delete ordering creating unrecoverable orphaned objects, the architect-review retry missing network-level errors, and operational tables (`audit_archive_manifest`, `audit_partition_config`) lacking TRUNCATE guards despite holding legally-critical state.
